title: Partial Calendar Truth
warm:
Partial calendar truth put [player_name] alone with Nolan Greer in the hallway between their doors, Rhea's thinning marks spoken aloud without Brooks yet holding the recorder. Weekly silk. Monthly politeness. Blank. Vivienne Greer's presence as schedule more than marriage, still not a settled fate—willing, paid, dead, or staging. Detective Imani Brooks waited somewhere below with homicide interest rising and no body required to make the air colder.

"I will not pretend monthly was ordinary," [player_name] said. Early thirties. Soft alibi cracking into something sharper. "I also will not hand you a corpse you have not confessed. Partial truth is the only honest temperature left."

Nolan's cufflinks clicked. Wind sheer. Elevator bank humming. Unused perfume leaked faintly from his penthouse crack like a third person listening. "Partial truth still feeds colder files. You can stay at Brooks's soft interview door long enough for the blowup—no relief, no Pell polish, just the detective's temper when cadence without ending refuses to become a charge. Or you go downstairs after Rhea and trace what burned in her grate when someone decided guest-log ash was safer than guest-log ink."

[player_name] tasted oak she had not drunk and fear she had. "Blowup keeps me in the room where soft interviews die. Ash keeps me in the building's throat where Rhea hides what money cannot fully buy. Neither writes Vivienne's ending. Both spend the romance we almost used as glue."

Marcus Pell was a missed call vibrating in Nolan's pocket. Black car memory idled. Crownspire sold privacy; Brooks was learning how to subpoena it. [player_name] looked at the man across the hall who might have made his wife disappear—or protected her from something worse—or both—and felt trust versus complicity wear her name.

"Choose," Nolan said quietly. "Stay for the badge's temper. Or follow the burn."

She thought of bringing Nolan to Brooks earlier—of soft interviews that still smiled—and how partial truth now arrived after those smiles had thinned. Crownspire's hush was becoming a timeline. Rhea's grate had smelled like panic when [player_name] passed desk last; ash was not metaphor. Someone had edited guest memory with fire. Brooks would call that obstruction. Nolan might call it protection. [player_name] had to decide which chase wore her name.

"If I stay for the blowup," she said, "I become the neighbor who watched soft die in real time. If I follow the burn, I become the neighbor who touched the building's throat. Soft alibi shrinks either way."

Nolan's answer was almost gentle. "Soft was always shrinking. We just kept pouring wine on it."

Crownspire's hush scored the choice. Soft alibi was never pink; soft meant pliable evidence—the mistress money preferred when a wife thinned to silence. [player_name] refused to become only that preference even while her body still answered Nolan's door. Brooks's escalating file, Rhea's eyes, Pell's letterhead, Vivienne's open fates: every pressure asked for a verb. She would give one. She would not give a corpse she had not seen.

Partial calendar truth was a blade with two dull edges: not enough for Brooks to charge, too much for Nolan to call traveling with a straight wrist. [player_name] had lived the cadence from across the hall—elevator chimes on nights Vivienne still came, silence on nights she did not, wine rings that might have been anyone's. Soft alibi had been built from those almosts. Now almosts were being asked to stand up in a colder file. Blowup at the interview door meant watching mercy die. Ash from Rhea's grate meant touching the building's panic. Neither was justice. Both were motion. Motion was what Layer 5 demanded when fate could not yet settle.
hot:
Partial calendar truth made the hallway feel like an unfinished undressing. [player_name] said weekly-to-monthly-to-gone against Nolan Greer's mouth-adjacent silence and felt his cufflink click like a finger on a clit she refused to offer yet. Soft alibi heat. Law pressure. Vivienne contested. Brooks rising toward homicide language without a corpse. Early thirties and shaking, across-the-hall geography turning twelve steps into a dare.

"Partial is all you get," she whispered, chest brushing his. "No invented body. No settled fate. Cadence only—while my body still wants yours stupid."

His hand hovered at her waist, heat without claim. "Stay at Brooks's door for the blowup—temper, no relief, soft interview dying with your nipples tight under interrogation light. Or chase Rhea's burned grate—ash on your fingers instead of me—while mid-want screams that evidence is a poor substitute for finishing this against your doorframe."

Elevator chime. Perfume ghost. She ached. Chose between badge temper and ash, consequence-verbs loud, climax deferred on purpose.

His hovering hand at her waist was a cruelty she leaned into. Blowup meant interrogation light on her flushed throat while he sat close enough to smell and not touch. Ash meant soot on her fingers she might later put in her mouth without thinking—filthy metaphor becoming literal taste. Partial calendar truth had made her wet and furious. She wanted to finish the hallway kiss and knew finishing belonged after consequence had a name. Vivienne's contested doors pressed her from one side; Brooks's temper from the other; Nolan's unfinished claim from the front. Choosing felt like picking which pressure got to leave a mark.

Heat advanced trust-versus-complicity rather than decorating fear. Her body kept score—thighs, breath, unfinished mouth—while law pressure climbed. Nolan remaining the only LI meant every throb had a name and a risk. She exited mid-want on purpose, Vivienne still contested, Brooks still rising, soft alibi still wearing her pulse.

She wanted to shove him against her door and make partial truth come out of his mouth between her legs—cadence as filthy catechism—and knew Brooks climbing the shaft made that fantasy into obstruction cosplay she refused to eroticize. Crime stayed plot. Heat stayed heat. The refusal itself aroused her in a bitter way: discipline as edging. Blowup light on her flushed cheeks. Ash on fingers she might later wrap around him. Mid-want invented futures while the hallway held only verbs.
